§11.2.4 Legend and Overlay Values

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-legend-and-overlay-values · charts types

✅ Normative

When a chart's values are printed only in its legend or as data labels over its marks, those printed numbers are the data: every one of them MUST be in the chart table, copied exactly. A companion series without printed values is estimated as usual — unless no printed label can locate its points, in which case it has no column (see Labels§11.1.2).

Values print in three places, and all three are treated the same (see Values and Tolerances§11.1.4):

Where the value prints What goes in the table
On or beside each mark — bar-top numbers, slice amounts, point callouts the printed value in the mark's cell
In the legend — Solar (45%)-style entries the name part as the row or column label, the number part as the value
At a direct label — a line end stating its value (see Line Charts§11.2.5) the printed value in the cell of that end position

✅ Sample — MonthlyTreasuryStatement_202509_p8


Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement — Figure 7 (public domain)

Twin pies sharing one legend, amounts printed beside the slices. Every slice name appears in both pies with a different value, so each pie is its own table under its own printed title, and the title is what tells them apart. Rows follow each pie clockwise from the top. The amounts are copied as printed — $1,581B with its separator, and ($60B), whose parentheses mark the Other slice of September as negative. The footnote under the legend is cut off at the bottom of the page and is elided.

✅ Sample — upstream_financial_review_2024_p9

A daily price curve with no printed name or values, and a triangle-marker series whose legend entry reads first-day-of-month price, all twelve of its values printed at the markers. The named series is the table's one column: 12 printed values, copied with their $. The daily curve has no printed name that could head a column — Jan alone also locates the marker series — so it gets no column. The two bold average statements are printed text, not data points, and follow the table.
